summary: The U.S. Air Force has officially placed its first hypersonic weapon, the Air-Launched Rapid Response Weapon, into production, marking a significant milestone for defense capabilities. In civil space developments, NASA has formally ended its Swift space telescope mission following an unsuccessful rescue attempt, even as the agency moves to overhaul its procurement process to launch science missions more frequently. Pre-flight preparations continue for NASA’s NEO Surveyor mission following inspections of its sunshade and solar cells, while researchers analyzing Perseverance rover data from Neretva Vallis reported new clues regarding Martian dust to help protect future human crews. In military space initiatives, the U.S. Space Force announced plans to have a cislunar surveillance payload ready for launch by 2029, which follows an Air Force Research Laboratory demonstration of orbital cargo transport alongside SpaceX. Within the commercial sector, satellite operator Astranis upgraded its launch contract with SpaceX to a dedicated Falcon 9 mission for its entire Block 4 fleet, French expansion began for Flexell Space via a new subsidiary, and startup Cowboy Space revealed plans for a data center rocket dubbed "Big Iron." In astrophysics, researchers utilizing the James Webb Space Telescope and ALMA identified a dusty, rapidly growing black hole in the early universe, while astronomers documented an unprecedented cosmic explosion that sustained activity for 27 days. Readers should keep an eye out for SpaceX’s next orbital Starship flight test following the recent static fire ignition of its Super Heavy booster engines.
